why_this_file_exists: SM-AI-I had NO floors file, so every one of its 52 exam-scope tasks defaulted to a floor of 8 while the bank held 7 to 9 per task. verify-cert's s8 check was therefore already failing on 9 (task, language) pairs BEFORE anything was retired, and PROMPT-147's 65 retirements took it to 72. The floors here are what the bank holds after that retirement.
the_rule: floor = the live, approved, SECURE row count for the task, counted per language and taken at the MINIMUM -- the same number verify-cert's s8 check compares a floor against. Derived from the BANK and not from a saturation census: the Scrum family has zero `task_sources` rows, so there is no map to derive an effective-primary count from and `propose-task-floors` correctly refuses. Written by `apply-task-floors.mjs --from-held`.
_what_this_floor_does_not_mean: It is NOT a statement that the task cannot hold more. Nothing has been generated for SM-AI-I, so every task could be refilled by authoring or by a grounded path once the family is mapped. The floor records what is served today so that a real shortfall is visible against it, instead of 52 tasks sitting permanently below a default nobody set.
